items.question: Why did BMO's CET1 ratio go down in fiscal 2025?
items.answer:
Short answer
- BMO’s CET1 Ratio fell from 13.6% to 13.3% in fiscal 2025. The bank says this was because internal capital generation was more than offset by (a) the purchase/cancellation of 22.2 million common shares and (b) higher source‑currency risk‑weighted assets (RWA) [S1][S2].

Key supporting facts from the filings
- Reported CET1 Ratio: 13.6% → 13.3% (Oct 31, 2024 → Oct 31, 2025) [S4][S5].
- CET1 capital (C$ millions) increased: C$57,054 → C$58,286 (Oct 31, 2024 → Oct 31, 2025) [S3].
- Risk‑weighted assets increased: C$420.8 billion → C$437.9 billion (Oct 31, 2024 → Oct 31, 2025) [S6].
- Management’s explanation: “Our CET1 Ratio decreased … as internal capital generation was more than offset by the impact of the purchase of 22.2 million common shares for cancellation and higher source currency risk‑weighted assets (RWA).” (MD&A) [S1][S2].

Additional context from the report
- The Tier 1 and Total Capital Ratios fell for the same reasons; the impact on Total Capital was partially offset by a higher provisioning excess due to a larger allowance for credit losses for accounting purposes versus the regulatory view [S1].
- RWA increase details: credit RWA up (net asset quality changes, asset growth, FX), market RWA up (portfolio changes/growth), operational RWA little changed [S6].

If you want a numeric decomposition of how much of the CET1‑ratio decline came from CET1 capital versus higher RWA, I can compute that — but I need access to the calculation tool (I must use it to perform arithmetic per the filing‑analysis rules).

items.question: What assets did Canadian Natural acquire from Chevron in December 2024, and what share of AOSP does it own after the deal?
items.answer:
Canadian Natural acquired Chevron Canada Limited’s Alberta assets in December 2024, including:
- a 70% operated working interest in the light crude oil and liquids‑rich Duvernay asset play in Alberta [S1][S2]; and
- a 20% interest in the Athabasca Oil Sands Project (AOSP) (the acquisiton also included various working interests in other non‑producing oil sands leases) [S1][S2][S4].

As a result of the acquisition, Canadian Natural’s combined direct and indirect working interest in AOSP is 90%. AOSP includes the Muskeg River and Jackpine mines, the Scotford Upgrader and the Quest Carbon Capture and Storage facility [S1][S2][S5].

Note: the filings contain differing statements of aggregate consideration for the acquisition (see flagged issue) [S1][S4].
